parts.name: Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instr: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.example: 0 — A undergone  B suffered  C passed  D survived → A
parts.title: Back on two wheels
paras: Over the past decade, cycling has (0) undergone a remarkable revival in many cities. Faced with traffic jams and rising fuel prices, more and more commuters have decided to [[1]] their cars at home and travel to work by bike.

City councils have been quick to [[2]] advantage of this trend by building separate cycle lanes and introducing bike-sharing schemes, which allow people to [[3]] up a bicycle at one station and leave it at another. In some places, the number of cyclists has more than doubled in just a few years.

It goes without [[4]] that cycling is cheap, keeps people fit and does not [[5]] the air. However, safety remains a serious [[6]]. Many people say they would cycle more often if they did not have to [[7]] the road with buses and lorries. Experts agree that the future of urban cycling will [[8]] largely on how safe it feels.

q.expl: leave sth at home — оставить дома. Let — позволять, put требует указания места действия (put sth somewhere), stay не берёт дополнения.
Устойчивое выражение take advantage of — воспользоваться. С make/get/have оно не образуется.
pick up — взять, забрать (велосипед на станции). Take up — заняться чем-то, set up — установить, get up — вставать.
Идиома it goes without saying that… — само собой разумеется, что…
pollute the air — загрязнять воздух. Stain — оставить пятно, poison — отравить (кого-то), waste — тратить впустую.
a serious concern — серьёзная проблема, повод для беспокойства. Care, interest и attention так не используются.
share the road with — делить дорогу с кем-то. Divide и split — делить на части, join — присоединиться.
depend on — зависеть от. Count on и lean on — рассчитывать на кого-то, trust — доверять (без on).

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Why do we yawn?
paras: Everyone yawns, but scientists still do not fully agree (0) on why we do it. For a long time, it was believed that yawning brought more oxygen into the body. However, experiments have shown that breathing extra oxygen does not make people yawn [[9]] often.

A more recent theory suggests that yawning helps to cool the brain. When we yawn, we take in a large amount of air, [[10]] may lower the temperature of the blood flowing to our heads. Supporters of this idea point [[11]] that we tend to yawn when we are tired, which is when the brain may be working least efficiently.

Perhaps the strangest thing about yawning is that it is contagious. Simply seeing someone else yawn, or even reading [[12]] yawning, can be enough to set us off. Interestingly, we are more likely to 'catch' a yawn from a family member [[13]] from a stranger. Some researchers believe this is linked to empathy – our ability to understand [[14]] other people are feeling. [[15]] this is true, it might explain why young children, who are still developing this ability, rarely catch yawns. So if you have yawned at least once [[16]] reading this, don't worry – it's perfectly normal.

q.expl: yawn more often — зевать чаще. Нужна сравнительная степень.
После запятой which относится ко всей мысли: «мы вдыхаем много воздуха, что может понизить температуру». That после запятой не ставится.
point out that… — указать на то, что…
read about sth — читать о чём-то.
Сравнение: more likely … than.
understand how other people are feeling — понимать, что чувствуют другие. Подойдёт и what.
Условие: If this is true, it might explain… — если это правда, это могло бы объяснить…
while reading this — пока читал это. Подойдут также when и since.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Never too late for music
paras: Many adults wish they had learned to play an instrument when they were young. The good news is that it is never too late. In fact, research suggests that learning music in later life can bring (0) considerable benefits.

Playing an instrument requires a great deal of [[17]], which keeps the brain active. It also improves [[18]] between the hands and eyes. For many people, however, the greatest reward is [[19]]: music offers a way to relax and to express feelings that are difficult to put into words.

Of course, adult learners face their own [[20]]. Busy work schedules can make regular practice [[21]] to fit in, and many people feel [[22]] about making mistakes in front of a teacher. Experts advise beginners to be [[23]] with themselves and to set [[24]] goals, such as learning one simple song a month.

q.expl: После a great deal of нужно существительное: concentration — сосредоточенность.
coordination between the hands and eyes — координация рук и глаз; нужно существительное.
После is здесь нужно прилагательное: the greatest reward is emotional — главная награда эмоциональная.
face their own challenges — сталкиваться со своими трудностями; множественное число (their own …).
make sth difficult — делать что-то трудным; после make + object нужно прилагательное.
Чувство человека: feel embarrassed — стесняться. Ловушка: embarrassing описывает ситуацию, а не человека.
be patient with yourself — быть терпеливым к себе.
realistic goals — реалистичные цели. Real goals — «настоящие цели», по смыслу не подходит.

parts.name: Key word transformation
parts.instr: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.
parts.example: 0 What type of music do you like best? FAVOURITE → What IS YOUR FAVOURITE type of music?

q.first: It's ages since I last went swimming.
q.expl: It's ages since I last did… ⇄ I haven't done… for ages.

q.first: The film was so good that we watched it twice.
q.expl: so + adj ⇄ such + a + adj + noun: such a good film.

q.first: I'm sure Mark is at home – his car is outside.
q.expl: Уверенность в настоящем: must be — должно быть, наверняка.

q.first: My brother is too young to drive.
q.expl: too young to ⇄ not old enough to. Enough ставится после прилагательного.

q.first: People say the restaurant is excellent.
q.expl: be supposed to be — говорят, что; считается, что.

q.first: Could you turn the music down, please?
q.expl: Вежливая просьба: Would you mind + -ing.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a teenage wildlife photographer. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: Through the lens
parts.subtitle: Sixteen-year-old Leo Grant has won a national award for wildlife photography. Kate Hill joined him on an early-morning shoot.
paras: It is half past four in the morning, and Leo Grant is lying on his stomach in a wet field, completely still. I am lying next to him, trying not to sneeze. We are waiting for a family of hares that, according to Leo, appear here most mornings just before sunrise. 'Most of wildlife photography is about being in the right place and then doing absolutely nothing,' he whispers. 'The hard part is not getting bored.'

Leo took his first wildlife pictures at the age of eleven, using his mum's old phone. 'They were terrible,' he laughs. 'Blurry ducks, mostly.' What changed everything was a free photography workshop at his local nature reserve. The ranger who ran it looked through Leo's pictures and, instead of praising them, told him exactly what was wrong with each one. 'Nobody had ever taken my photos that seriously before. I went home and practised every day for a month.'

His winning photograph shows a fox crossing a frozen river at dawn, its breath visible in the cold air. Leo spent eleven mornings at the same spot before he got the shot. 'People assume it's luck,' he says, 'and there is some luck involved. But you make your own luck by turning up again and again.' He admits that on several of those mornings he nearly stayed in bed. 'My alarm would go off, and every part of me wanted to ignore it.'

Winning the award has brought some unexpected attention. A local newspaper ran a story about him, and he has since been asked to give talks at several schools. Leo is clearly uncomfortable with the fuss. 'I'm not really a public speaker,' he says, looking at his boots. 'But if one kid goes out and looks at a bird properly because of me, it's worth feeling awkward for an hour.'

Just as the sun begins to rise, the hares appear – three of them, chasing each other across the grass. Leo's camera clicks quietly. Afterwards, he shows me the pictures on the screen, and I am surprised to see that he has already deleted most of them. 'If I keep everything, I never look at anything properly,' he explains. 'One good picture is better than a hundred average ones.' As we walk back to the car, soaked and freezing, he is already planning tomorrow's shoot.

q.stem: What does Leo say is the most difficult part of wildlife photography?
q.hl: The hard part is not getting bored.
q.expl: Самое трудное — не заскучать, пока долго ничего не происходит. Ранний подъём и холод упоминаются в тексте, но трудностью Лео называет именно это.

q.stem: Why was the workshop at the nature reserve important to Leo?
opts: It gave him access to better equipment.
He received honest criticism that motivated him.
The ranger praised his natural talent.
It was the first time he had photographed wild animals.
q.hl: Nobody had ever taken my photos that seriously before.
q.expl: Рейнджер не хвалил, а разобрал ошибки на каждом снимке, и это мотивировало Лео тренироваться месяц. Ловушка C: «instead of praising them».

q.stem: What does Leo suggest about his prize-winning photograph?
opts: It was taken almost by accident.
Its success depended mainly on persistence.
He would not have taken it without help.
He regrets the time he spent getting it.
q.hl: But you make your own luck by turning up again and again.
q.expl: Одиннадцать утр на одном месте: удачу «делаешь сам», приходя снова и снова. Удача есть (A), но главное — упорство.

q.stem: How does Leo feel about giving talks at schools?
opts: He enjoys being the centre of attention.
He finds it uncomfortable but thinks it is worthwhile.
He thinks it takes too much time away from photography.
He would prefer to talk to adults.
q.hl: it's worth feeling awkward for an hour
q.expl: Ему неловко, но если хоть один ребёнок начнёт смотреть на птиц, это того стоит.

q.stem: Why does Leo delete most of his pictures?
opts: His camera does not have enough storage.
He wants to focus only on his best work.
He is rarely satisfied with anything he does.
He has already photographed hares many times.
q.hl: One good picture is better than a hundred average ones.
q.expl: Если хранить всё, ничего толком не рассмотришь; один хороший снимок лучше сотни средних.

q.stem: What impression does the writer give of Leo in the article as a whole?
opts: He is dedicated to his work and modest about his success.
He is sure that he will become a professional photographer.
He prefers working alone to sharing his knowledge.
He takes great risks to get the perfect picture.
q.hl: Leo is clearly uncomfortable with the fuss.
q.expl: Весь текст: ранние подъёмы, одиннадцать утр ради кадра, планы на завтра — преданность делу; неловкость от внимания — скромность. О профессиональных планах (B) не сказано, знаниями он делится (C).

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a man who ran his first half-marathon. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: Running for beginners
parts.subtitle: A year ago, Tom Harris couldn't run for a bus. Last month, he finished his first half-marathon.
paras: At school, I was always the last to be picked for any team. I hated sport, and running in particular. [[37]] So nobody was more surprised than me when, at the age of twenty-nine, I signed up for a half-marathon.

The decision wasn't exactly planned. A colleague was collecting money for a children's hospital, and after a conversation that I only half remember, I agreed to run with her team. [[38]] By then, it was too late to back out: I had already told everyone at work.

My first training run lasted eleven minutes, and I had to stop and walk three times. I came home red-faced and convinced I had made a terrible mistake. [[39]] She told me to forget about speed completely and simply aim to run a little further each week.

Slowly, things began to change. After two months, I could run for half an hour without stopping. [[40]] I had always assumed that runners were naturally fit people who found it easy, but most of the people there were just like me.

The race itself was a blur. The first ten kilometres went well, but at around fifteen kilometres my legs started to feel like concrete. [[41]] Strangers lining the route were shouting my name, which was printed on my shirt, and somehow that kept me going.

I finished in two hours and twenty-three minutes – hardly a record, but I didn't care. Together, our team raised more than three thousand pounds for the hospital. [[42]] I've already signed up for next year's race, and this time, I'm aiming to beat my own time.

sents.A: Cross-country lessons in the rain were my idea of torture.
sents.B: It was only the next morning that I realised what I had done.
sents.C: Fortunately, my colleague had been running for years and knew exactly what to say.
sents.D: I even joined a local running club, something I had always been too embarrassed to do.
sents.E: I seriously considered stopping and walking the rest of the way.
sents.F: And I discovered something I never expected to say: I'm a runner.
sents.G: The weather forecast for race day had been terrible, but in the end it stayed dry.

q.expl: Продолжение «I hated sport, and running in particular»: кросс под дождём был пыткой (A). Дальше контраст «So nobody was more surprised…».
Разговор он «помнит наполовину», и только наутро понял, что натворил (B). «By then, it was too late» связывает с «next morning».
«She told me…» — нужно предложение, где появляется женщина: опытная коллега, которая знала, что сказать (C).
«most of the people there» — где? В беговом клубе, куда он вступил (D).
Ноги как бетон → всерьёз думал остановиться (E) → но прохожие кричали его имя, и это помогло дойти.
Итог истории: он понял, что стал бегуном (F), и уже записался на следующий забег. Ловушка G: погода к пропуску не подходит, перед этим речь уже о финише и деньгах.

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article in which four people describe an unusual job. For questions 43–52, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: Not your usual nine-to-five

texts.name: Nina, video game tester
texts.body: People think I play games all day for fun, but testing is very different. I might spend a whole week walking into the same wall in different ways to see if the character gets stuck. It's repetitive, and you need a lot of patience. The best part is when a game I've worked on is released and I see players enjoying it, knowing I helped get rid of hundreds of problems they'll never know existed. I got the job after sending the company a list of bugs I'd found in one of their games – a cheeky way to apply, I suppose, but it worked.

texts.name: Omar, zookeeper
texts.body: My day starts at seven with cleaning – the part of the job that nobody ever films for television. Then come the feeds, health checks and keeping the animals busy so they don't get bored; we hide food in boxes, for example. I've been bitten twice, both times because I wasn't paying attention, so I've learned to respect every animal, however friendly it looks. The pay isn't great, and I work most weekends, but I can't imagine doing anything else.

texts.name: Grace, food stylist
texts.body: I make food look delicious for photographs and adverts. It's harder than it sounds – ice cream melts under studio lights in seconds, so we sometimes use mashed potato instead. I trained as a chef, but I got tired of the long nights in restaurant kitchens. A photographer I met at a friend's wedding suggested I try styling, and I've never looked back. The only downside is that I'm never allowed to eat what I make – it's usually been sprayed with something to keep it shiny.

texts.name: Ben, mattress tester
texts.body: My job is to test mattresses for a big furniture company. Yes, I'm paid to lie down – my friends never let me forget it. In reality, it's quite scientific: I fill in detailed reports about comfort, temperature and how my back feels after a night. I have to sleep in a different bed most nights, which sounds fun until you've done it for a month. What I didn't expect was how much I'd miss my own bed. I've started taking my own pillow with me everywhere.

q.stem: got their job by contacting an employer in an unusual way?
q.hl: I got the job after sending the company a list of bugs I'd found in one of their games
q.expl: Нина отправила компании список ошибок в их же игре.

q.stem: changed career after a chance meeting?
q.hl: A photographer I met at a friend's wedding suggested I try styling
q.expl: Грейс встретила фотографа на свадьбе друга, и он посоветовал попробовать.

q.stem: is often teased by friends about their job?
q.hl: my friends never let me forget it
q.expl: Друзья Бена постоянно шутят, что ему платят за то, что он лежит.

q.stem: mentions a part of the job that the public rarely sees?
q.hl: the part of the job that nobody ever films for television
q.expl: Уборку, по словам Омара, никогда не показывают по телевизору.

q.stem: learned a lesson from their own carelessness?
q.hl: both times because I wasn't paying attention
q.expl: Омара кусали, когда он был невнимателен, и он научился уважать каждое животное.

q.stem: says that the job requires a lot of patience?
q.hl: you need a lot of patience
q.expl: Нине неделями приходится повторять одно и то же.

q.stem: uses a substitute to solve a practical problem?
q.hl: we sometimes use mashed potato instead
q.expl: Мороженое тает под лампами, поэтому вместо него берут картофельное пюре.

q.stem: takes satisfaction in work that others do not notice?
q.hl: hundreds of problems they'll never know existed
q.expl: Нина рада, что игроки даже не узнают о сотнях исправленных ошибок.

q.stem: accepts disadvantages because they love what they do?
q.hl: The pay isn't great, and I work most weekends, but I can't imagine doing anything else
q.expl: Платят мало и почти все выходные рабочие, но Омар не представляет другой работы. Ловушка C: у Грейс тоже есть минус, но она не говорит, что мирится с ним из любви к работе.

q.stem: has developed a habit to cope with a disadvantage of the job?
q.hl: I've started taking my own pillow with me everywhere
q.expl: Бен скучает по своей кровати и возит с собой подушку.
